confirmed_blocking.summary: The FR-010 re-entry marker check reads a ledger that `factory show` does not return, so a prior retro spawn can never be detected.
confirmed_blocking.evidence: commands.py digest() puts 'ledger' in LARGE and emits only spawns: {total: N}; step 5.1 says 'If its ledger already has an entry with stage retro, skip to item 4'. FR-010 requires no second spawn on re-entry. ENG-15.
confirmed_blocking.fix: Read the marker from the run's state.json ledger (path is in show's state_path) or expose a bounded retro-spawn marker in the show digest, and update SKILL.md step 5.1 accordingly.

confirmed_blocking.summary: claim reads, checks and replaces a backlog entry without the home-level lock that add holds, so a claim landing between add's scan and replace is overwritten back to ready.
confirmed_blocking.evidence: add() acquires lock.acquire(directory, harness='improvements') around scan+write (lines 66-175); claim() (lines 253-285) does read/status-check/_write_atomic with no lock. add then writes status 'ready', claimed_at null over a claimed own-run entry, violating FR-016/plan item 3 ('claimed ... never overwritten') and the plan's single-writer lock constraint. ENG-23, ENG-26.
confirmed_blocking.fix: Wrap claim's read-check-write in the same lock.acquire/release on <home>/improvements (with the same bounded wait), and add a test for the interleaving/serialization.

confirmed_blocking.summary: Retro entry filenames use only the repo basename and branch, so two distinct repositories with the same basename and branch target the same file and can replace another run's claimed entry.
confirmed_blocking.evidence: backlog_name() uses Path(repo).name (line 34); ownership at line 94 compares the full repo path. A claimed entry from repo A is neither 'own' nor 'covered' (covered only tracks ready) for repo B, so B's add replaces it at lines 149-168. plan.md settled item 1 asserts names are 'unique and injective'; FR-016 derives names from the source run. ENG-26.
confirmed_blocking.fix: Make the retro filename identity distinguish source repositories (e.g. a short stable hash of the full repo path), or refuse to replace an existing destination whose run.repo differs; update DESIGN.md/plan naming and tests consistently.

confirmed_blocking.summary: The confirmed S1 failure path 'unwritable improvements/ exits 1 with no temp debris' is not genuinely exercised: the test makes improvements/ a regular file so add fails at mkdir before any temp write.
confirmed_blocking.evidence: test_add_unwritable_directory_reports_path_without_temp replaces the directory with a file; directory.mkdir raises before _write_atomic, and the *.tmp assertion checks home/, not improvements/. _write_atomic's cleanup, preservation of earlier writes and reporting of completed writes are untested. Plan Confirmed scope lists this path; ENG-1, ENG-4, ENG-18.
confirmed_blocking.fix: Add a deterministic CLI-level test with a real writable-then-failing improvements/ (e.g. read-only directory or injected replace failure) asserting exit 1, path in stderr, reported prior writes, an unchanged existing entry, and no *.tmp inside improvements/.

advisory.summary: ENG-26: retro ledger intervals land after ended_at, so totals.compute can report agent_ms beyond wall_ms (overhead clamped to 0); the run export predates retro records. No requirement broken — FR-016 requires the export unchanged.
advisory.fix: Document or adjust post-pr-open accounting (e.g. extend the wall bound to the last ledger end) and add a totals assertion.

advisory.summary: ENG-24: the retro retry says 'same inputs', which reuses the first spawn's possibly expired deadline, conflicting with the Time budget policy's fresh `budget <role>` before every SPAWN.
advisory.fix: Run `factory budget retro` again before the retry and pass the new deadline.

advisory.summary: ENG-25: branch is used unencoded in the filename. Traversal is not reachable via git branch names (git forbids '..'), and the writer-owned state.json is a local trust boundary; a legal 'a/b' branch would make the write fail (same as the pre-existing export).
advisory.fix: Encode or reject path separators in branch/repo components and assert the destination's parent is improvements/.

advisory.summary: ENG-25: `--detail "<error>"` interpolation into a SHELL line repeats the pre-existing failure-policy pattern (unchanged line 173); not introduced by this change, but a literal-argument convention would be safer.
advisory.fix: Instruct single-quoting/escaping of agent error text, or pass detail via a file/stdin, across all issue-add uses.

advisory.summary: ENG-24: --from is read whole with no byte or candidate-count bound; input is the orchestrator's own saved envelope, so risk is low.
advisory.fix: Require a regular file, cap bytes before parsing and cap candidate count before validation.

advisory.summary: A parseable done envelope with retro.candidates missing or not a list is treated as zero candidates and is never retried or named in the final notice; protocol.md defines the field as optional, so this is a spec ambiguity against US3 and SC-001 rather than a clear violation.
advisory.fix: Treat a done retro envelope without a retro.candidates list as malformed (retry/skip-notice path), and make the field required on done retro envelopes in protocol.md.

advisory.summary: S4 wording says 'no edit tools for every harness', but codex cannot express tool restrictions and is already excluded by the documented disclosure in ReadOnlyConformanceTests; the test asserts what each harness can enforce.
advisory.fix: Reconcile plan S4 wording with the codex disclosure (scoped limitation) rather than adding an unenforceable assertion.
